report:
The three sisters have agreed on a path forward. All three confirmed the steps in the shared list.

The family list
1. C will not sign off on A buying the family house at a family discount, and she wants B to receive her share. Raised by C.
2. C would accept A buying at an independently established fair market value, or a sale to someone else, with the proceeds handled according to the will. Raised by C.
3. A wants to buy the house with her husband and will not move ahead without C's agreement. Raised by A.
4. B wants a fair arrangement that leaves her some money to start her dance studio, and wants clarity soon. Raised by B.
5. No sister has confirmed that the will was read with all three present, and none has a copy. Raised by C.
6. A would consider a jointly chosen independent valuation and will ask a lender or broker what she and her husband could borrow in principle. Raised by A.
7. B will ask the lawyer for a copy of the will and will not name an amount until she has seen it. Raised by B.
8. C will join B in asking the lawyer for the will. Raised by C.
9. A and C both agree the valuer should be chosen jointly, and both hold off on who pays for the valuation until the will and the amount are known. Raised by A and C.
10. B will also ask the lawyer who is named executor and whether the estate can cover the valuation. Raised by B.

What is settled: no sale at a family discount, and A accepts she cannot proceed without C's agreement. B and C will send the lawyer one joint letter asking for a copy of the will for each sister, the name of the executor, and whether the estate can pay for an independent valuation. A will get an in-principle borrowing figure and will take the will to her own lawyer before agreeing any price. Once the will arrives, the three of them will choose a valuer jointly and move to valuation.

What is still open: B has not named the amount she needs for her dance studio, A does not yet know whether she and her husband can fund two thirds of the value, and who pays for the valuation depends on the will. I gave no legal advice and moved no money. My last message to each sister set out her next step.
